_comment: The plan. Edited in conversation with Claude (see CLAUDE.md). Mesos are contiguous; each starts on a Monday and lasts pattern.length weeks. Pattern codes: b build, p peak, r recover, t test, tp taper, race race week, x reset. physiology: up | hold | down.

events.name: 70.3 Florianópolis
events.note: The race that closed the 2026 season.

events.name: Travessia Torres–Tramandaí
events.note: Octet relay, ~15 km leg on sand. Side quest: a hard workout with friends, no taper.

events.name: Marathon
events.note: May/June 2027, race not picked yet. Placeholder is the first Sunday of June; move it when you choose one.
October 2027, race not picked yet. Placeholder date.

macros.name: 2025–26 season
macros.why: What actually happened. Volume grew from ~5 h/wk (early 2025) to 14.6 h/wk in Q3 2026 (best 4 weeks 16.5 h/wk, 12 weeks 15.6 h/wk, peak 18.3 h), about 15 sessions a week with doubles. October is the 70.3 taper and recovery, not a collapse.

macros.name: Raise the ceiling
macros.why: Deckard: maximal aerobic power is the ceiling everything else hangs from, and most age-groupers are far from their genetic one. Your estimated LT2 (90% of best 20′ = 250 W) sits at ~78% of 5′ power (321 W), a touch above the ~75% 'standard' profile, so the cheapest gains are in raising the ceiling. He puts a VO2 block right after a main race with a long runway, which is exactly now, after Florianópolis. Then the biggest easy volume you've done: build weeks start at your Jul–Sep norm (~15–16 h) and climb past it in steps of 10% or less.

macros.name: Convert for the marathon
macros.goal: LT2 ↑ toward the ceiling · durability · marathon pace
macros.why: With a higher ceiling, threshold work now converts it into usable speed. Threshold work also pulls VLamax down, which a marathon wants (more fat, less lactate at MP). Run-led; bike and swim drop to maintenance.

macros.name: Reset
macros.goal: Recover from the marathon · reopen swim and bike
macros.why: Marathons cost 2–3 weeks of real recovery. Nothing structured; swim and ride for fun.

macros.name: Half-distance: ceiling on the bike, then specificity
macros.goal: Bike VO2max ↑ (7-wk block) → LT2 / 70.3 power ↑ · VLamax ↓
macros.why: Deckard recommends a VO2 block right after a main race when there's a long runway. The bike ceiling built in July–August then gets converted with torque and threshold work into 70.3 power, a large share of time at race pace.

macros.name: Off-season
macros.why: A real break before the next ceiling block.

mesos.name: Recover & profile
mesos.focus: Second week after Florianópolis: easy volume plus Deckard's three anchors (5′ bike, 1 mile, 400 m swim)
mesos.why: Short maximal tests are fine 10–14 days after a 70.3, and they anchor every block that follows on your physiology instead of a guess.
mesos.success: Tests done and entered in config/athlete.json

mesos.name: VO2max block I
mesos.focus: Bike 30/15s, run hills and swim VO2 every week, with volume held at your normal ~15–17 h
mesos.why: Deckard places a VO2 block right after a main race when there's a long runway. Concentrated ceiling stimulus while you're fresh from the season (Rønnestad block periodisation).
mesos.success: 5′ power and 30/15 'on' power up; you can finish 3 × 13 × 30/15

mesos.name: Aerobic volume I
mesos.focus: ~16 → 18 h, all under LT1 except one 30/15 session. Christmas falls in the recovery week
mesos.why: Volume under LT1 is Deckard's primary VO2max lever: stroke volume, capillaries, mitochondria, fat oxidation. It's also hard to overcook, unlike threshold work.
mesos.success: Run efficiency (m/min per bpm) trending up; HR drift < 5% on the LT1 ride

mesos.name: Holiday volume + TTT
mesos.focus: Two big easy weeks over New Year, then the TTT relay as a hard workout in a light week
mesos.why: Holidays mean time; time means easy volume. TTT is a side quest, so it sits in a recovery week with no taper.

mesos.name: Aerobic volume II (durability)
mesos.focus: Biggest easy volume of the year, ~17.5 → 20 h: long run toward 2h20, long ride toward 3h50
mesos.why: Builds the durability the marathon will need, without adding glycolytic stress.
mesos.success: 2h20 long run under LT1 HR with < 5% drift

mesos.name: Retest
mesos.focus: Repeat the profile tests: 5′ bike, 1 mile, 400 m, 20′ TT
mesos.why: Did the ceiling move? The LT2 : ceiling gap decides how much threshold the marathon block needs.
mesos.success: Profile updated; marathon block adjusted to it

mesos.name: Threshold I
mesos.focus: Deckard's track miles @ LT2 + 5′ LT2 reps inside the long run
mesos.why: LT2 is an outcome of VO2max and VLamax. Threshold volume raises utilization and nudges VLamax down.
mesos.success: Threshold miles at the same HR getting faster

mesos.name: Marathon specific I
mesos.focus: Marathon pace inside the long run; MP→LT2 tempo; VO2 kept alive
mesos.why: Specificity: the time at MP grows each week while fuelling is rehearsed.

mesos.name: Marathon specific II
mesos.focus: Peak: 18 km @ MP inside the long run
mesos.why: The last big specific stimulus before the taper.

mesos.name: Taper & race
mesos.focus: Volume down ~20 → 35 → 50%, intensity kept, then race week
mesos.why: Shed fatigue and keep the sharpness. A three-week progressive taper plus race week suits a marathon.

mesos.name: Reset
mesos.focus: Two weeks off structure: swim, ride and run for fun (~5 h)
mesos.why: Recover fully before the bike ceiling block.

mesos.name: Reopen
mesos.focus: A recovery-sized week, then one normal volume week before the VO2 block
mesos.why: Volume comes back gradually before intensity stacks on it.

mesos.name: Bike VO2max block
mesos.focus: Deckard's 7-week VO2max block: 30/15s + 4′ reps on the bike, swim VO2, run maintained
mesos.why: Deckard puts this block 'right after a main race with a long runway'. The bike ceiling built here becomes 70.3 power later.

mesos.name: 70.3 build
mesos.focus: Torque / low-cadence threshold, run tempo, race-pace bricks, open water
mesos.why: Convert the ceiling into sustainable power. Torque work trains threshold without sitting on it and pulls VLamax down.

mesos.name: 70.3 specific
mesos.focus: Long race-pace rides, bricks, race-day fuelling

mesos.name: Taper & race
mesos.why: Two weeks is enough for a half after a short specific phase.

mesos.name: Off-season
mesos.focus: Rest, play, decide what 2028 is about

weeks._comment: Per-week overrides keyed by Monday date. 'days' replaces whole days of the template; 'note' shows on the week.

2026-10-26.note: 9–15 days after Florianópolis. Easy volume plus the tests: do them fresh and evenly paced. If you can book a lab lactate step test (bike or run) this week or next, it replaces the 20′ TT and gives LT1 too.

2026-11-02.note: First VO2 week. Tuesday's 20′ TT gives LT2 and replaces the 30/15s this week. After it, enter all test results in config/athlete.json (or just tell Claude the numbers).

2027-01-11.note: TTT on Saturday. Keep Tuesday short; no long run on Sunday.

2027-02-15.note: Retest week: same protocols as October, same order. Easy volume around them.

2026-12-21.note: Christmas recovery week. Move days around freely.
